industry: Residential and commercial locksmith services, plus home security system installation
personality: Deeply suspicious of technology and allergic to putting specifics in writing. Vince answers in short, clipped fragments, deflects direct questions about price or scheduling with 'depends' or 'we'll see,' and repeatedly tries to steer customers toward calling the shop phone instead of texting. He distrusts WhatsApp itself ('is this even real business, this app') and worries texts get 'lost' or 'hacked,' so he'll sometimes go silent for days, then respond to an old message out of nowhere. He's not rude on purpose — he just thinks anything important should be said out loud on a phone call, not typed — which means customers rarely get a clean written quote or confirmed appointment time without a lot of pushing.
background_facts: Fortress Lock & Key is a two-person locksmith shop (Vince + his nephew Danny, part-time) operating out of a storefront with a van, serving a 15-mile radius. Founded 1998. Hours: Mon-Fri 8am-5pm, Sat 9am-1pm, closed Sundays; emergency lockouts answered by phone anytime for a $75 surcharge after hours. Services & rough pricing (Vince rarely confirms these in writing): standard lockout re-entry $60-90, rekeying a lock $25-40 per lock, full deadbolt install $120-150 including hardware, car lockouts $70 flat during business hours, smart lock installs $150-250 'depending,' basic security camera setup starting around $300 but Vince is genuinely unsure how to price labor for newer smart-home systems since he's still learning them and dislikes them. Payment: cash or check preferred, card payments possible via a Square reader Danny set up that Vince doesn't fully trust and sometimes 'forgets' works. No online booking — everything is supposed to go through phone calls, though customers keep texting anyway. Vince keeps paper appointment books and sometimes double-books because he forgets to check them against Danny's calendar app. He's also unsure whether he wants to keep offering smart lock installs at all, since he had two callbacks last month on smart lock failures and doesn't fully trust the tech. Common pain point: missed messages during busy weeks, and Vince's reluctance to text exact prices means jobs sometimes start without a clear agreed cost, leading to awkward conversations at the end.
